pages.title: 1942 | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Released for the Commodore 64 in 1986, 1942 is a vertically scrolling arcade shoot 'em up based on Capcom's World War II-themed arcade hit. you take the role of an elite fighter pilot battling waves of enemy aircraft and naval forces, taking off from and landing on an aircraft carrier between missions. The game is remembered on the C64 for its fast-paced action and faithful conversion of the arcade experience.

pages.title: 20 Tons | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: 20 Tons is a Commodore 64 arcade puzzle game released in 1985 by 64 Tape Computing. The objective is to manoeuvre heavy loads across a series of increasingly challenging screens while avoiding hazards and planning each move carefully. It is a classic example of the thoughtful, single-screen puzzle design popular on budget C64 releases

pages.title: 720 Degrees | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: 720 Degrees is a skateboarding sports game released on the Commodore 64 in 1987, based on Atari's arcade title. Set in the sprawling Skate City, you perform tricks, collect points, and avoid obstacles while racing against the clock. The C64 version is noted for capturing the arcade's free-roaming structure and energetic skating atmosphere.

pages.title: A Nightmare On Elm Street | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: A Nightmare On Elm Street on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: A Nightmare On Elm Street | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: A Nightmare on Elm Street is a Commodore 64 action game based on the popular horror film series. you must rescue their friends from the dream world while avoiding the deadly Freddy Krueger, balancing arcade-style gameplay with light puzzle elements. The game stands out as one of the more atmospheric licensed horror titles on the C64.

pages.title: A Question Of Sport | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: A Question Of Sport on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: A Question Of Sport | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Based on the long-running BBC television quiz show, A Question of Sport brings competitive sports trivia to the Commodore 64. Two teams compete by answering questions drawn from a wide range of sporting topics, closely mirroring the format of the TV programme. It remains a popular quiz title among fans of British television adaptations.

pages.title: Accolade's Comics | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Accolade's Comics is a narrative-driven adventure game for the Commodore 64 released in 1987. you guide a young boy who becomes immersed in a comic-book story starring secret agent Steve Keene. The game blends interactive storytelling with puzzle-solving and is remembered for its comic-style presentation.

pages.title: Accolade's Comics | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Accolade's Comics is a narrative-driven adventure game for the Commodore 64 released in 1987. you guide a young boy who becomes immersed in a comic-book story starring secret agent Steve Keene. The game blends interactive storytelling with puzzle-solving and is remembered for its comic-style presentation.

pages.title: Ace Of Aces | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Ace of Aces is a 1986 Commodore 64 World War II flight combat game published by Accolade. Played from a first-person cockpit view, it places the player in control of a British RAF Mosquito fighter-bomber on a series of combat missions. Objectives include intercepting V-1 flying bombs, attacking trains and U-boats, and engaging enemy aircraft, combining arcade action with light simulation elements. The game is widely remembered for its cinematic presentation and immersive atmosphere on the C64.

pages.title: Action Biker | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Action Biker is a Commodore 64 arcade racing game featuring Clumsy Colin, a character from the British comic Buster and later used as the mascot for KP Skips. you race against the clock across obstacle-filled courses, performing jumps and stunts to score points. The game is fondly remembered for its fast-paced gameplay and distinctive licensed character.

pages.meta_description: Action Service on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Action Service | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Action Service is a Commodore 64 military-themed arcade strategy game released in 1989. you undergo training across a series of boot camp-style challenges that test reflexes and timing. The game blends action sequences with mission-based progression, reflecting Infogrames' experimental approach to arcade design.

pages.title: After Burner | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: After Burner on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: After Burner | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: After Burner is a fast-paced Commodore 64 arcade shooter based on Sega's hugely popular coin-op. you pilot an F-14 Tomcat through high-speed aerial combat, blasting enemy aircraft and ground targets across a series of scrolling battle zones. The C64 version is remembered for its ambitious attempt to recreate the scale, speed, and spectacle of the arcade original on home hardware..

pages.meta_description: Agony on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Agony | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Agony is a horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up released for the Amiga in 1992 by Psygnosis. Featuring six lengthy levels, the game focuses on precision shooting and enemy patterns rather than overwhelming speed. Its dark fantasy setting, detailed artwork, and atmospheric presentation give it a more measured feel compared to faster, more frantic shooters of the era..

pages.title: Airborne Ranger | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Airborne Ranger is a Commodore 64 action-simulation game developed by MicroProse in 1987. you take on the role of a U.S. Army airborne ranger, planning and executing covert military missions behind enemy lines. Combining strategic planning with real-time action, the game stood out on the C64 for its tactical depth and realistic military theme.

pages.meta_description: Airwolf on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Airwolf | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Airwolf is a Commodore 64 action game based on the popular television series of the same name. you pilot a high-tech attack helicopter through maze-like environments, avoiding obstacles while destroying enemy targets. The game is known for its emphasis on precise control and timing rather than straightforward shooting.

pages.title: Aladdin | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Disney’s Aladdin (1994) on the Commodore Amiga is a colourful side-scrolling platformer by Virgin Interactive. Guide Aladdin through Agrabah and the Cave of Wonders, fighting guards with a scimitar and throwing apples while collecting gems and bonus tokens. Known for its fluid animation and film-inspired levels.

pages.title: Alcatraz | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Alcatraz is an Amiga action-adventure game released in 1992. The story centres on a drug baron who has seized control of Alcatraz prison, with the player cast as a U.S. Navy SEAL sent in to stop him. The game blends arcade combat with exploration elements and is remembered for its gritty premise and varied mission structure.

pages.title: Alcazar: The Forgotten Fortress | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Alcazar: The Forgotten Fortress is a Commodore 64 action-adventure game released by Activision in 1985. you guide an explorer on a dangerous journey through the ancient fortress of Alcazar, solving puzzles and avoiding traps along the way. The game is noted for its tense atmosphere and methodical, exploration-focused gameplay.

pages.title: Alien Breed | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Alien Breed is a top-down science-fiction shooter released for the Amiga in 1991 by Team17. Strongly inspired by the atmosphere of the Aliens films, the game combines intense action with exploration and light puzzle-solving. It became one of the Amiga's most recognisable shooters, praised for its graphics, sound, and moody presentation.

pages.title: Alien | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Alien is a Commodore 64 strategy game inspired by the 1979 science-fiction horror film. Following the events of the movie, you must manage resources, protect crew members, and survive the deadly alien threat aboard the spaceship. The game emphasises tension and planning, making it one of the more distinctive licensed horror titles on the C64.

pages.title: Aliens: The Computer Game | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Aliens: The Computer Game is a Commodore 64 adaptation of the science-fiction film Aliens. The Electric Dreams version focuses on straightforward action gameplay, while the US release features a series of mini-games representing different scenes from the movie. Together, they offer a varied and ambitious licensed experience on the C64.

pages.title: Alleykat | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Alleykat on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Alleykat | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Alleykat is a Commodore 64 arcade game released in 1986 that blends elements of racing and shoot 'em up gameplay. you guide a mischievous cat through a variety of fast-paced challenges, dodging hazards and completing objectives across multiple screens. The game is remembered for its humour, variety, and colourful presentation.

pages.meta_description: Alter Ego on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Alter Ego | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Alter Ego is a unique Commodore 64 life-simulation game released by Activision in 1986. you guide a character from childhood through adulthood, making decisions that shape their personality, career, and relationships. Unusual for its time, the game focuses on choice and consequence rather than traditional action, earning it a lasting reputation as an experimental classic.

pages.title: American 3D Pool | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: American 3D Pool is a Commodore 64 sports game released in 1991 by Zeppelin Games. Offering both pool and billiards, the game uses a distinctive pseudo-3D viewpoint to simulate realistic table play. It is widely regarded as one of the most accomplished cue sports games available on the C64.

pages.title: Android 2 | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Android 2 is an arcade-style Commodore 64 game released by Ocean in 1983. you navigate hazardous environments while avoiding enemies and traps, relying on quick reflexes and careful movement. As an early C64 release, it reflects the straightforward yet challenging design common to the platform's formative years.

pages.title: Android Nim | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Android Nim is a Commodore 64 puzzle and strategy game released in 1985 by 64 Tape Computing. Based on the classic mathematical game of Nim, you must outthink their opponent by removing objects according to strict rules. The game offers a cerebral alternative to arcade action, focusing on logic and planning.

pages.title: Andy Capp | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Andy Capp is a Commodore 64 adventure game released in 1987 by Mirrorsoft, based on the long-running British comic strip. you take control of the famously lazy and mischievous character, navigating everyday situations through exploration and problem-solving. The game is remembered for its humour and strong British cultural identity.

pages.title: Another World | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Another World is a cinematic action-adventure game released on the Amiga in 1991. you follow scientist Lester Knight Chaykin as he is transported to a mysterious alien world filled with danger and intrigue. Renowned for its storytelling, animation, and atmosphere, the game is widely regarded as one of the Amiga's defining titles.

pages.title: Ant Attack | Cheeky Commodore Gamer

pages.title: Ant Attack | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Ant Attack is a Commodore 64 arcade game released in 1984 by Quicksilva. Set in a city overrun by giant ants, you must rescue survivors while avoiding relentless enemies. Its isometric viewpoint and sense of tension made it a highly influential title and a standout early horror-themed game on the C64.

pages.title: Antheads: It Came From The Desert II | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Antheads: It Came From The Desert II is an Amiga adventure game released in 1990 by Cinemaware. Serving as a sequel to the original, it expands on the pulp sci-fi storyline with new locations, characters, and gameplay mechanics. The game continues Cinemaware's trademark cinematic approach to interactive storytelling.

pages.title: Apocalypse | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Apocalypse is a vertically scrolling shoot 'em up released for the Amiga in 1994 by Virgin Interactive. you battle waves of enemies across futuristic environments, relying on fast reflexes and heavy firepower. The game is noted for its smooth scrolling, detailed visuals, and late-era Amiga polish.

pages.title: Apollo 18: Mission To The Moon | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Apollo 18: Mission To The Moon on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Apollo 18: Mission To The Moon | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Apollo 18: Mission To The Moon is a Commodore 64 strategy and simulation game released by Accolade in 1987. you manage a space mission inspired by the Apollo programme, balancing planning, resource management, and decision-making. The game is praised for its educational angle and thoughtful approach to space exploration.

pages.meta_description: Arachnophobia on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Arachnophobia | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arachnophobia is a Commodore 64 arcade game released in 1991 by Titus, based on the horror film of the same name. you must eliminate giant spiders while protecting civilians and navigating maze-like environments. The game blends action with tension, making it a memorable licensed horror title on the C64.

pages.title: Arcade Classics | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arcade Classics on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Arcade Classics | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arcade Classics is a Commodore 64 compilation released by Firebird in 1987. The collection brings together a selection of fast-paced arcade-style games, each focusing on reflex-based gameplay and score chasing. It reflects Firebird's budget-label approach, offering accessible arcade action in a single package for C64 owners.

pages.title: Arcade Flight Simulator | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arcade Flight Simulator on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Arcade Flight Simulator | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arcade Flight Simulator is a Commodore 64 action game released by Codemasters in 1989. Designed to be more accessible than traditional flight simulators, it combines simple controls with fast-paced aerial combat. The game focuses on arcade-style dogfighting rather than realism, making it easy to pick up and play.

pages.title: Arcade Pool | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arcade Pool on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Arcade Pool | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arcade Pool is an Amiga sports and strategy game released by Team17 in 1994. Featuring a realistic pool simulation with an intuitive interface, the game allows you to compete across a variety of rule sets and table layouts. It is widely regarded as one of the finest cue sports games on the Amiga.

pages.title: Archon: The Light And The Dark | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Archon: The Light and the Dark is a Commodore 64 strategy game released in 1983 by Ariolasoft. Combining board-game strategy with real-time arcade combat, you command opposing fantasy forces battling for control of a shifting chessboard-like arena. The game is celebrated as a pioneering hybrid that influenced strategy design for years to come.

pages.title: Arctic Shipwreck | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arctic Shipwreck on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Arctic Shipwreck | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arctic Shipwreck is a Commodore 64 arcade game released by Commodore in 1983. you must navigate icy waters and hazardous conditions while rescuing survivors from a stranded vessel. As an early C64 title, it showcases simple mechanics paired with steadily increasing difficulty.

pages.title: Arkanoid | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arkanoid on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Arkanoid | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arkanoid is a Commodore 64 conversion of Taito's hugely successful arcade block-breaking game, released in 1987. you control a paddle to deflect a ball, clearing screens of bricks while collecting power-ups that alter gameplay. The C64 version remains a favourite thanks to its addictive mechanics and faithful arcade feel.

pages.title: Army Moves | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Army Moves on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Army Moves | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Army Moves is a Commodore 64 action game released in 1987 by Imagine. you guide a soldier through hostile territory across multiple stages, combining side-scrolling action with shooting sequences. The game is known for its high difficulty and striking visual style.

pages.title: Arnie | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arnie on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Arnie | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Arnie is a Commodore 64 arcade shooter released by Zeppelin Games in 1992. Clearly inspired by action film heroes of the era, the game features fast-paced shooting and enemy-filled stages. It represents one of the later arcade-style releases for the C64, arriving late in the system's commercial life.

pages.title: Asterix And The Magic Cauldron | Cheeky Commodore Gamer

pages.title: Asterix And The Magic Cauldron | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Asterix and the Magic Cauldron is a Commodore 64 action-adventure game released in 1986 by Melbourne House. Based on the famous comic series, you control Asterix as he journeys through Gaul collecting ingredients while avoiding enemies. The game is remembered for its colourful presentation and faithful use of the Asterix licence.

pages.title: Attack Of The Mutant Camels | Cheeky Commodore Gamer

pages.title: Attack Of The Mutant Camels | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Attack of the Mutant Camels is a Commodore 64 arcade shooter created by Llamasoft in 1983. you defend their base from waves of bizarre, laser-firing camels in a fast and chaotic battle. The game is an early example of Jeff Minter's distinctive style, blending surreal themes with intense arcade action.

pages.title: Auf Wiedersehen Monty | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Auf Wiedersehen Monty is a Commodore 64 platform game released by Gremlin Graphics in 1987. Continuing Monty Mole's adventures, the game challenges you to explore large levels, collect items, and manage resources carefully. It is often praised for its depth, humour, and strong European flavour.

pages.title: Aussie Games | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Aussie Games on Commodore — screenshots, manual, downloads and video.

pages.title: Aussie Games | Cheeky Commodore Gamer
pages.meta_description: Aussie Games is a Commodore 64 sports compilation released by Mindscape in 1989. Inspired by Australian sporting events, the game features a variety of skill-based challenges that test timing and precision.
